# Couchwire 0.2.3: A fix for a black screen
*23 November 2026*
Fixes a black screen when the PS5 turns down the first request to start a stream.
### Fixed
- The stream no longer stays black when the PS5 turns down the first request and Couchwire quietly tries again. The picture was arriving, but the window kept showing the first try's empty video.
**Update:** Couchwire 0.1.0 and later offer this update by themselves; or choose **Couchwire › Check for Updates…**. New here? Download `Couchwire-0.2.3.dmg`, open it, and drag Couchwire onto Applications. Needs macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon. The app is not notarised, so the first time macOS may say it cannot verify it: open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the message about Couchwire and click **Open Anyway**.
**Source:** Couchwire is free software under the GNU AGPL v3. `Couchwire-0.2.3-source.tar.gz` is the source of this release, including chiaki-ng, and `Couchwire-0.2.3-dependencies-source.tar` holds the exact sources of the libraries it's built with.

# Couchwire 0.2.2: Smoother on mobile data, sharper at home
*23 November 2026*
Automatic smoothing adds far less delay on a mobile hotspot, automatic quality gets back to full quality faster and can reach 50 Mbps at home, and Couchwire no longer quits while connecting over the internet.
### Added
- **Play on mobile data, with port forwarding.** Some mobile networks block internet play (Sony's app too). If you forward the PS5's ports on your home router, enter your home's address under **Away from Home** in the console's settings, and Couchwire connects straight to it, waking the PS5 first. - **Setup asks for the PS button.** When a controller is connected during setup, macOS asks whether Couchwire can respond to the PS button, and setup explains to click Allow.
### Changed
- **Automatic smoothing** no longer assumes the worst on mobile hotspots. It starts at Balanced and steps up to Steadiest only while frames keep arriving very late, then steps back down after a calm minute. On a steady hotspot that roughly halves the delay. - **Automatic quality climbs back faster.** After a session at home with a short, steady connection and nothing lost, it goes straight back to 1080p at 30 Mbps instead of one step at a time. - **Automatic quality can reach 50 Mbps at home.** After a smooth session at 30 Mbps on your home network, wired or Wi-Fi, it moves up to 50 Mbps, if your own settings allow it. Over the internet it stays at 30 Mbps at most. - A tidier **About Couchwire** window. - While connecting over the internet, Couchwire keeps libchiaki's detailed connection log, so slow or failed connections can be looked into. It asks a busy PS5 again after 8 seconds instead of 12. - The system log now records whether a stream is HDR at each step (what the PS5 sends, the decoded frames and the display's HDR headroom), and each change automatic quality makes. - The PS button tip and setup use a controller symbol instead of the PlayStation logo.
### Fixed
- **Lower Quality** no longer fails over the internet. The PS5 takes up to a minute to let go of the old stream, so Couchwire now keeps asking, as it does after a network change, and says it's restarting at lower quality. - Couchwire no longer quits while connecting over the internet. On some networks it opens 250 sockets at once to find a way through, which used up macOS's limit of 256 for an app.
**Update:** Couchwire 0.1.0 and later offer this update by themselves; or choose **Couchwire › Check for Updates…**. New here? Download `Couchwire-0.2.2.dmg`, open it, and drag Couchwire onto Applications. Needs macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon. The app is not notarised, so the first time macOS may say it cannot verify it: open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the message about Couchwire and click **Open Anyway**.
**Source:** Couchwire is free software under the GNU AGPL v3. `Couchwire-0.2.2-source.tar.gz` is the source of this release, including chiaki-ng, and `Couchwire-0.2.2-dependencies-source.tar` holds the exact sources of the libraries it's built with.

# Couchwire 0.2.1: The PS button, and a tidier Settings
*23 November 2026*
The PS button can now go to your PS5 instead of opening Games on your Mac, Settings fits on a laptop screen, and the sound recovers faster after Wi-Fi trouble at home.
### Changed
- Settings is split into Video, Account and Updates tabs, so it fits on a laptop screen. Internet Play is under Account.
### Fixed
- On a network that won't allow a direct connection to your PS5 (some mobile networks), Couchwire now says so after two tries instead of retrying for two minutes. - The connecting steps no longer say they're waking your PS5 when it's already on. After a network change they say they're reconnecting, explain the wait while the PS5 lets go of the old stream, and number each new try. - After a burst of Wi-Fi trouble at home (for example when your Mac scans for a hotspot), the sound catches up with the picture within about half a minute, instead of trailing it for several minutes.
### Added
- The first time you stream with a DualSense or another controller with a Home button, Couchwire explains how to send the PS button to your PS5 instead of opening Games on your Mac, with a button that opens Game Controllers settings. - Couchwire writes a line of performance stats to the system log every 10 seconds while streaming, and logs each connect, wake-up and error message, so slow or failed connections can be looked into afterwards.
**If the PS button opens Games on your Mac:** open System Settings › Game Controllers and add Couchwire to **Home Button Overrides**. Couchwire shows this tip the first time you stream with a controller.
**Update:** Couchwire 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 offer this update by themselves; or choose **Couchwire › Check for Updates…**. New here? Download `Couchwire-0.2.1.dmg`, open it, and drag Couchwire onto Applications. Needs macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon. The app is not notarised, so the first time macOS may say it cannot verify it: open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the message about Couchwire and click **Open Anyway**.
**Source:** Couchwire is free software under the GNU AGPL v3. `Couchwire-0.2.1-source.tar.gz` is the source of this release, including chiaki-ng, and `Couchwire-0.2.1-dependencies-source.tar` holds the exact sources of the libraries it's built with.
